articles.title: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term
articles.mainIdea: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term
articles.summary: Argus Research: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term. We have aggregated data from 20 of Wall Street's largest firms, and their year-end 2026 S&P 500 (SPX) targets range from a low of 7,000 to a high of 8,100. As such, the most bullish call on the Street is for a very respectable 17% gain from Friday's close, while the most bearish is forecasting a flat year. The median SPX forecast is 7,700 while the average estimate is 7,635, some 10% to 11%, respectively, above current levels. We recently compiled various technical potential targets, and they ranged from 7,300 to near 7,900. But they were for the highs of 2026 and not for the end of next year. As always, targets are, at best, guesstimates and are subject to change, largely due to price action. Recall that back during the "tariff tantrum" in March and April, many of the 2025 bulls threw in the towel and lowered their 2025 year-end targets -- only to raise them back up once the dust settled. Back then, things indeed were looking grim and prices were cascading quickly. So becoming less bullish during that period of huge uncertainty seemed like a logical approach. Looking back, it was all just a massive head fake from the stock market. Currently, we are in the weakest historical period of the presidential cycle (November 2025-October 2026), which could mean a pullback/correction in 2026. When is the most likely period for this typical cycle weakness? There is a consistent 34-week to 36-week cycle for the market, and the next top is due in the late April. The most-recent cycle top led to a flat market, while prior cycle tops in December 2024, April 2024, July 2023, and March 2022 worked out well. (Mark Arbeter, CMT) Related tickers mentioned: ILMN.
